sections.title: THERE IS A MDT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS COASTAL SC/NC
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST/MID-ATLANTIC STATES...

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A PROGRESSIVE LONGWAVE PATTERN WILL REMAIN OVER THE CONUS DURING THE PERIOD...HIGHLIGHTED BY AN ACTIVE SOUTHERN STREAM FROM THE SOUTHWEST STATES/ROCKIES TO THE MID-ATLANTIC/SOUTHEAST STATES. MOST RELEVANT FOR DEEP CONVECTIVE POTENTIAL IS A CLOSED TROUGH CENTERED OVER THE MID-SOUTH/TN VALLEY EARLY TODAY AND AN ASSOCIATED 100+ KT POLAR JET STREAK /250-300 MB/ TRANSLATING EASTWARD OVER THE GULF COAST REGION. THIS UPPER TROUGH WILL BECOME INCREASINGLY CLOSED/NEGATIVELY TILTED AS IT REACHES THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION BY TONIGHT. SEVERE POTENTIAL TODAY WILL BE FOCUSED ACROSS THE CAROLINAS/SOUTHEAST STATES NEAR/AHEAD OF AN EASTWARD MOVING COLD FRONT.

sections.title: CAROLINAS/SOUTHEAST VA
sections.text: A STRONG/POTENTIALLY SEVERE QLCS WILL LIKELY BE ONGOING THIS MORNING ACROSS PORTIONS OF GA/NORTH FL...WITH A LESS VIGOROUS PORTION OF THE QLCS/ASSOCIATED COLD POOL LIKELY TO BE LOCATED ACROSS THE SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS VICINITY AND UPSTATE PORTIONS OF THE CAROLINAS. WHILE AN EARLY DAY SEVERE THREAT MAY EXIST...A MORE ORGANIZED/SUSTAINED SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO MATERIALIZE MAINLY ACROSS COASTAL/PIEDMONT PORTIONS OF THE CAROLINAS BY THIS AFTERNOON. IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE INCREASINGLY CLOSED/NEGATIVELY TILTED UPPER TROUGH AND ASSOCIATED UPPER JET EXIT REGION/STRONG HEIGHT FALLS...AMPLE DYNAMIC FORCING FOR ASCENT AND VERY STRONG VERTICAL SHEAR /50-80 KT 0-6 KM/ WILL STEADILY OVERSPREAD THE REGION TODAY. WHILE THE PRIMARY SURFACE LOW MAY MOVE DEVELOP NEAR/JUST WEST OF THE APPALACHIANS...A SECONDARY SURFACE LOW SEEMS LIKELY TO DEVELOP/SPREAD NORTHEASTWARD IN THE IMMEDIATE LEE OF THE APPALACHIANS/PIEDMONT VICINITY OF THE CAROLINAS INTO SOUTHEAST VA AND EVENTUALLY THE DELMARVA VICINITY. THIS SCENARIO WILL SUPPORT AN INFLUX OF A RELATIVELY MOIST ATLANTIC AIRMASS IN TANDEM WITH A NORTHWARD MOVING WARM FRONT...WITH LOWER 60S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS LIKELY TO BECOME ESTABLISHED ESPECIALLY ACR

sections.title: GA AND NORTHERN/CENTRAL FL
sections.text: A THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO WILL EXIST TODAY IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE ONGOING QLCS/NEAR-COLD FRONTAL CORRIDOR ACROSS GA INTO NORTHERN/CENTRAL FL. THE RISK IS EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY DIMINISH WITH SOUTHWARD EXTENT ACROSS FL AS THE PRIMARY DYNAMIC FORCING FOR ASCENT SLOWLY SPREADS AWAY FROM THE REGION LATER THIS AFTERNOON. ..GUYER/SMITH.. 12/26/2012

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A NEGATIVELY-TILTED MIDLEVEL TROUGH OVER THE TN VALLEY INTO CNTRL/ERN GULF STATES WILL EJECT NEWD TO OFF THE ATLANTIC COAST BY THE END OF THE D1 PERIOD IN RESPONSE TO THE AMPLIFICATION OF THE NEXT UPSTREAM TROUGH OVER THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST. SIGNIFICANT 500-MB HEIGHT FALLS OF 150-180M/12HR WILL SPREAD NEWD ACROSS THE CAROLINAS AND VA TODAY IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE FORMER SYSTEM MENTIONED ABOVE. IN THE LOW LEVELS...AN OCCLUDING SURFACE LOW OVER NERN TN WILL DEVELOP NEWD INTO THE CNTRL APPALACHIANS...STEADILY WEAKENING WITH TIME. CONCURRENT CYCLOGENESIS IS FORECAST THIS MORNING OVER UPSTATE SC WITH THIS FEATURE PROGRESSING TO ERN VA BY 27/00Z...AND TO OFF THE NJ COAST BY THE END OF THE D1 PERIOD. THIS SECONDARY LOW WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY A RETREATING WEDGE/WARM FRONT WHICH WILL MOVE NWD THROUGH THE CNTRL/ERN CAROLINAS AND INTO THE DELMARVA LATER TONIGHT. MEANWHILE...A STRONG COLD FRONT INITIALLY FROM THE SRN APPALACHIANS INTO THE FL BIG BEND WILL SWEEP EWD/NEWD TO OFF THE ATLANTIC SEABOARD.

sections.title: CAROLINAS/SERN VA TODAY
sections.text: A 50+ KT SLY LLJ CURRENTLY FROM THE NERN GOM INTO WRN CAROLINAS WILL MIGRATE NEWD IN TANDEM WITH THE UPPER SYSTEM. THE LLJ COUPLED WITH THE DEVELOPING SURFACE LOW IN THE LEE OF THE APPALACHIANS WILL HASTEN NWD FLUX OF AN INCREASINGLY MOIST PBL OFF THE ERN GOM AND ATLANTIC WITH DEWPOINTS RISING INTO THE LOWER 60S WITHIN THE SURFACE WARM SECTOR. WEAK MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES... WIDESPREAD CLOUDS...AND LINGERING PRECIPITATION WILL TEMPER THE DEGREE OF AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION...THOUGH THE INCREASING LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE SHOULD STILL BOOST MLCAPE VALUES TO 500-1000 J/KG. CURRENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT TSTMS WILL INCREASE IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY LATER THIS MORNING ALONG/AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT ACROSS UPSTATE SC AND WRN/CNTRL NC AS DEEP-LAYER ASCENT BEGINS TO OVERSPREAD AN INCREASINGLY MOIST AND UNSTABLE AIR MASS DEVELOPING INLAND. A CONCURRENT INCREASE IN STORMS IS EXPECTED NEARER TO THE NERN SC/NC COASTS WHERE LOW-LEVEL CONFLUENCE IS ENHANCED WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR. BY THIS AFTERNOON...ONE OR MULTIPLE BANDS OF SEVERE TSTMS WILL RAPIDLY ADVANCE THROUGH ERN NC AHEAD OF THE EJECTING UPPER TROUGH. FORECAST HODOGRAPHS AND PLAN VIEW KINEMATIC FIELDS INDICATE INTENSE SHEAR IN LOW-LEVELS /E.G. EFFEC

sections.title: SERN GA/FL
sections.text: A CONVECTIVE BAND WITH EMBEDDED TSTMS FROM JUST W OF AYS TO NEAR CTY AND INTO THE NERN GOM AS OF 12Z WILL PROGRESS EWD/SEWD ACROSS THE REGION TODAY. WHILE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL REMAIN STRONG...LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL GRADUALLY WEAKEN WITH TIME AS THE LLJ LIFTS N OF THE REGION. MOREOVER...A CAP AT THE BASE OF AN EML AS SAMPLED BY THE 12Z TAMPA SOUNDING MAY LIMIT UPDRAFT STRENGTH/VIGOR...ESPECIALLY AS LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT DIMINISHES. WHILE LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND/OR A BRIEF TORNADO REMAIN POSSIBLE TODAY...THE THREAT APPEARS TO HAVE DIMINISHED SUFFICIENTLY THAT THE CATEGORICAL SLIGHT RISK HAS BEEN REMOVED. ..MEAD/LEITMAN.. 12/26/2012

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS PORTIONS ERN CAROLINAS
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... UPPER-AIR PATTERN WILL REMAIN PROGRESSIVE THROUGH PERIOD...FEATURING HIGH-AMPLITUDE-PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVES INITIALLY OVER SIERRA NEVADA REGION...AND FROM LOWER OH VALLEY SWD ACROSS MID TN AND AL. LATTER/ERN PERTURBATION CONTAINS CLOSED 500-MB CYCLONE...CENTERED AT 15Z OVER W-CENTRAL KY. ASSOCIATED TROUGH WILL ASSUME MORE NEGATIVE TILT WITH TIME...REACHING LE...MD PANHANDLE AND ERN NC BY 00Z. TROUGH SHOULD EXTEND FROM SERN ONT ACROSS PA TO DE BAY REGION BY 12Z. MEANWHILE...LEADING PORTION OF WRN TROUGH WILL REACH ERN CO AND NERN NM. AT SFC...INITIAL/OCCLUDED CYCLONE WAS CENTERED OVER ERN KY AT 15Z...WITH FRONTAL TRIPLE POINT FARTHER SE OVER CENTRAL SC. COLD FRONT EXTENDED SSWWD FROM THERE ACROSS SERN GA AND FL COASTAL BEND REGION OVER ERN GULF. WARM FRONT WAS DRAWN EWD ACROSS ERN SC TO NEAR ILM...THEN NEWD ROUGHLY ALONG COAST OVER HSE AREA. WARM FRONT MAY ADVANCE INLAND 50-75 NM BEFORE MAIN CONVECTIVE/CONVERGENCE BAND PASSES...FOLLOWED QUICKLY BY COLD FRONT.

sections.title: ERN CAROLINAS
sections.text: PREFRONTAL BAND OF STG-SVR TSTMS IS FCST TO CONTINUE GRADUAL INTENSIFICATION AS IT TRANSLATES EWD ACROSS REMAINDER OUTLOOK AREA THROUGH AFTERNOON...BEFORE MOVING OFFSHORE. TORNADO AND SVR WIND THREATS SHOULD INCREASE WITH PROXIMITY TO ATLC COAST...WHERE RICHEST BOUNDARY-LAYER THETAE WILL BE JUXTAPOSED WITH STRENGTHENING DEEP-SHEAR FIELDS ALONG AND S OF WARM FRONT. REF SPC WW 699 AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR LATEST NEAR-TERM GUIDANCE. ANTECEDENT STABILIZING EFFECTS OF CONSIDERABLE CLOUDS/PRECIP EFFECTIVELY HAVE IMPEDED NWD/INLAND PROGRESS OF SFC WARM FRONT AND WILL CONTINUE TO DO SO...WHILE ALSO RESTRICTING DIABATIC/DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION OF INLAND PORTIONS OF WARM SECTOR. WHILE THIS DEFINITELY DOES NOT PRECLUDE SVR...IT DOES REDUCE POTENTIAL COVERAGE/DENSITY OF THREAT ENOUGH TO LOWER OUR UNCONDITIONAL PROBABILITIES ATTM. DOING SO ALSO BRINGS DOWN OUTLOOK CATEGORY ONE NOTCH INTO SLGT RISK. NONETHELESS...SOMEWHAT ENHANCED DAMAGING WIND PROBABILITIES AND RISK FOR A SIGNIFICANT TORNADO SHOULD BE MAINTAINED GIVEN AT LEAST MRGL SFC-BASED BUOYANCY AND STRENGTH OF ENVIRONMENTAL WIND FIELDS -- YIELDING 50-60 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDE AND 300-500 J/KG EFFECTIVE SRH ALONG WARM FR

sections.title: CENTRAL/NRN FL
sections.text: BAND OF STG TSTMS IS EXPECTED TO MOVE EWD/SEWD ACROSS THIS REGION THROUGH AFTN...OFFERING POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED STG-SVR GUSTS AND VERY CONDITIONAL/QLCS-TYPE TORNADO POSSIBILITY. DIURNAL HEATING WILL INCREASE PREFRONTAL BUOYANCY FOR SEVERAL MORE HOURS...AND DEEP-LAYER SPEED SHEAR WILL REMAIN FAVORABLE. HOWEVER...NEWD DEPARTURE OF UPPER TROUGH AND RELATED DEEP-LAYER SUPPORT AWAY FROM AREA WILL CONTRIBUTE TO WEAKENING CONVERGENCE ALONG BOUNDARY AND DECREASE IN LOW-LEVEL SHEAR. ..EDWARDS/COHEN.. 12/26/2012

sections.title: ERN NC
sections.text: SURFACE ANALYSIS CONTINUES TO SHOW STRONG PRESSURE FALLS NEAR THE SURFACE LOW AS WELL AS N OF THE WARM FRONT WHICH EXTENDED EWD ACROSS CNTRL NC AT 19Z. EXTREMELY STRONG SHEAR PROFILES REMAIN IN PLACE ACROSS THE REGION WITH THE MAIN LIMITING FACTOR BEING INSTABILITY. THE BEST AREA FOR TORNADIC SUPERCELLS WILL CONTINUE TO BE NEAR THE NC COAST AND EXTENDING A FEW COUNTIES NWD TO THE WARM FRONT BEFORE THE COLD FRONT SWEEPS EWD WITH PERHAPS A THREAT OF SEVERE WIND.

sections.title: CNTRL FL
sections.text: FORCING ALONG THE TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO BE SUFFICIENT TO MAINTAIN A LINE OF THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON. THESE STORMS HAVE NOT SHOWN SIGNS OF BEING SEVERE...BUT A STRONG TO SEVERE WIND GUST MAY STILL OCCUR...AS WELL AS SMALL HAIL. THE STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO BE HAMPERED BY A CAPPING INVERSION AS WELL AS DRYING ALOFT AS THE UPPER SYSTEM BECOMES FARTHER REMOVED FROM THE REGION. ..JEWELL.. 12/26/2012 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1028 AM CST WED DEC 26 2012/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTMS MAY INCREASE IN INTENSITY BY 16Z IN ADVANCE OF A COLD FRONT AND DEVELOPING AREA OF LOW PRESSURE. ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS WILL FAVOR SUPERCELL AND BOWING STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS AND TORNADOES. A WW MAY BE NEEDED PRIOR TO 16Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A WARM FRONT EXTENDED FROM JUST S OF MRH INLAND NEAR MYR AND TO A DEVELOPING SECONDARY AREA OF LOW PRESSURE OVER NRN GA. AS THE MORNING PROGRESSES THE WARM FRONT WILL LIFT NWD IN TANDEM WITH THE DEVELOPING SFC LOW...RESULTING IN A MODESTLY UNSTABLE AND STRONGLY SHEARED ATM OVER CENTRAL/ERN SC AND SRN NC. WIDESPREAD CLOUDS AND PRECIPITATION WILL PREVENT SUBSTANTIAL DESTABILIZATION...HOWEVER COOLING MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES AND FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH A STRONG SHORTWAVE WILL FOSTER THE DEVELOPMENT/INTENSIFICATION OF TSTMS DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS OVER THE DISCUSSION AREA. VERY STRONG LOW-LEVEL WIND FIELDS HAVE RESULTED IN 0-1 KM SRH VALUES IN EXCESS OF 500 M2/S2...AND SUPERCELL STRUCTURES/BOWING SEGMENTS APPEAR INCREASINGLY LIKELY WITH A RISK OF TORNADOES AND DAMAGING WINDS. HIGH-RESOLUTION NUMERICAL GUIDANCE DEPICTS THIS SCENARIO UNFOLDING ACROSS THE DISCUSSION AREA THROUGH MIDDAY. CONVECTIVE TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR A WW PRIOR TO 16Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: GREATEST TORNADO THREAT IS EXPECTED TO BE GENERALLY CONTAINED TO COASTAL PORTIONS OF ERN NC AS OFFSHORE SUPERCELLS TRACK NNEWD REACHING AREAS TO THE NORTHEAST OF ILM THROUGH 22Z. FARTHER INLAND...DAMAGING WINDS SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY THREAT WITH ACTIVITY CURRENTLY EXTENDING FROM SAMPSON TO WILSON COUNTIES...AND AS IT TRACKS NNE/NE TOWARD FAR NERN NC/FAR SERN VA BY 2030-21Z. A NEW WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED TO THE NNE OF WW 699...DUE TO SPATIOTEMPORAL LIMITATIONS AND CONDITIONAL NATURE OF THREAT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 18Z...SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWED AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE HAD CONTINUED TO MOVE NEWD SINCE THIS MORNING AND WAS LOCATED OVER SOUTH CENTRAL-SERN NC /NEAR POPE AFB/. THE WARM FRONT MOVED INLAND AS FORECAST AND CURRENTLY EXTENDED EWD FROM THE LOW TO 15 S KGSB...AND THEN ENEWD THROUGH NERN NC TO THE S OF KECG. THE WARM SECTOR WAS DEMARCATED ON THE W BY THE COLD FRONT WHICH EXTENDED SWD THROUGH FAR ERN SC. HOWEVER...EXTENSIVE CLOUDS/PRECIPITATION ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR HAS LIMITED THE GREATEST DESTABILIZATION TO OFFSHORE AND COASTAL AREAS OF NC TO FAR ERN SC. IN THESE LATTER AREAS...REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY HAS CONTINUED TO SHOW ROTATING LOW LEVEL COUPLETS OFFSHORE. AS THESE STORMS TRACK NNEWD WITHIN LEADING CONFLUENT ZONES WHERE ACTIVITY WILL BE IN STRONGER INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE SRH OF 200-350 M2/S2...A TORNADO OR TWO CANNOT BE RULED OUT. MEANWHILE...A NNE-SSW LINE OF STORMS LOCATED FARTHER INLAND FROM EDGECOMBE TO SAMPSON COUNTIES NC. THIS ACTIVITY...DESPITE MEAGER INSTABILITY...IS LIKELY BEING MAINTAINED BY STRONG FORCING FOR ASCENT WITHIN THE LEADING EDGE OF THE DRY SLOT/DPVA ATTENDANT TO THE UPPER TROUGH AS IT BECOMES MORE NEGATIVELY TILTED. THE NRN EXTENT OF THESE STORMS SHOULD REACH FAR NERN NC/FAR SERN VA BETWEEN 2030-21Z. DAMAGING WINDS SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY THREAT WITH THIS ACTIVITY AS IT TRACKS QUICKLY NNEWD/NEWD. IF THE WARM FRONT WERE TO REACH THIS AREA PRIOR TO 2030Z...THEN A BRIEF TORNADO THREAT COULD NOT BE RULED OUT. ..PETERS.. 12/26/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A BROKEN BAND OF LOW-TOPPED CONVECTION/TSTMS HAS FORMED IN THE PAST HOUR ALONG COLD FRONT IN NORTHEAST NC. WERE THIS ACTIVITY TO CONTINUE TO STRENGTHEN...THE STORMS COULD POSE A RISK FOR MARGINALLY SVR HAIL...ISOLD DMGG WIND GUSTS...AND/OR A TORNADO THROUGH EARLY TNGT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A BROKEN BAND OF LOW-TOPPED SHOWERS AND STORMS HAS FORMED IN THE PAST HOUR ALONG AND AHEAD OF SHALLOW COLD FRONT PROGRESSING E ACROSS SE VA AND ERN NC. THE CONVECTION SHOULD CONTINUE TO MOVE E WITH THE FRONT AS THE BOUNDARY ADVANCES EWD IN ASSOCIATION WITH DEVELOPING SECONDARY CYCLONE NOW FORMING OVER THE LWR CHESAPEAKE BAY /PER AREA SFC WIND AND PRESSURE CHANGE DATA/. CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ALSO LIKELY IS BEING ASSISTED BY THE LEADING EDGE OF STRONGER MID-LVL COLD ADVECTION JUST NOW MOVING INTO REGION IN ASSOCIATION WITH VORT LOBE ROTATING THROUGH BASE OF LARGER-SCALE CNTRL APPALACHIANS TROUGH. AREA WIND PROFILES SHOW STRONG...LARGELY UNIDIRECTIONAL DEEP SWLY FLOW...WITH 700 MB SPEEDS ATTM AROUND 50 KTS. WIND PROFILES SHOULD REMAIN FAVORABLE FOR SUSTAINED STORMS/SUPERCELLS OVER SE VA/NE NC THROUGH MID EVE...ALTHOUGH SPEEDS SHOULD SOMEWHAT SLACKEN WITH THE APPROACH OF THE TROUGH. AT ANY RATE...IF THE UPDRAFTS NOW PRESENT ARE ABLE TO CONSOLIDATE INTO SUSTAINED STORMS...SOME POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR MARGINALLY SVR HAIL...LOCALLY DMGG WIND...AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. AREAL AND TEMPORAL EXTENT OF THIS RISK WILL...HOWEVER...BE TEMPERED BY STRENGTH OF SHEAR /ENTRAINMENT EFFECTS/...TIME OF DAY...AND FACT THAT AREA OVER WHICH STORMS WILL BE MOVING HAS BEEN SOMEWHAT STABILIZED IN THE LWR-LVLS BY PREVIOUS STORMS. THE CONVECTION/STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED. PARTS OF NE NC AND SE VA MAY REQUIRE A SMALL WW IF THE ACTIVITY SHOWS CONTINUOUS SIGNS OF STRENGTHENING/ORGANIZATION.
